newsitem.title: USA: Boy dies after police at G7 site try to help him.
newsitem.headline: Boy dies after police at G7 site try to help him.

text.p: A 17-year-old boy was shot in Denver's streets and died of his wounds ahead of the Group of Seven summit despite efforts by police guarding a key summit site to save his life, police said on Thursday.

Jason Paiz, 17, was pronounced dead at Denver Health Medical Centre Wednesday night after friends driving him to a hospital suddenly stopped in front of the Denver public library when they spotted a group of police cars.
Witnesses said police called an ambulance and summoned more squad cars to the scene, fearing that a drive-by shooting had taken place at the library, the main summit venue.
A friend of Paiz's, Jerry Lewis, 22, was also shot, police said. No arrests have been made and police are looking for a young man aged between 18 and 20 in connection with the shooting.

Security has been stepped up in Denver as leaders of the G7 -- France, Germany, Britain, Japan, Canada, Italy and the United States -- are joined by Russian President Boris Yeltsin for the meeting starting Friday, billed as The Summit of the Eight.
